method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Compilation register id C2016C00614 (latest amendment listed: 11 Feb 2016), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/C2004A01214.txt (retrieved 13 October 2026). Not deposited: Spam Regulations 2021 (encoded as adding nothing); the value of a penalty unit (Crimes Act 1914 s 4AA), so penalties are in penalty units

checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: From the seat of the consumer receiving marketing messages: s 5 (electronic message; voice calls on a standard telephone service excluded); s 6(1)(d)-(o) (commercial electronic message, purposes as facts); s 7(a)-(d) (Australian link); Schedule 1 cll 2-4 (designated: factual information; government bodies, registered political parties and registered charities about their own goods or services; educational institutions to enrolled students and households); Schedule 2 cll 2, 4, 6 (express, inferred and conspicuous-publication consent; withdrawal at the end of 5 business days, with a weekday table); s 16(1)-(5) (did the sender need my consent; mistake and ignorance of the link conditional); s 17(1) (sender identification, 30 days); s 18(1), (3), (9) (functional unsubscribe facility, 30 days); from the sender's seat, s 25(3)-(6) maximum penalties and Schedule 3 cl 5 infringement notice amounts, in penalty units. Not encoded: s 7(e); s 16(6); ancillary contraventions; Part 3 address harvesting; ss 24, 26-29; Parts 5-7; the rest of Schedule 3; the Spam Regulations 2021; public holidays in the business-day count.
seat: the consumer receiving marketing messages (the relevant electronic account-holder); the sender only for s 25 and Schedule 3
